name: Hardware-generic megakernel design
scope: Generality audit of how a megakernel compiler should parametrize itself by GPU target (SM80 cp.async/mma.sync; SM90 TMA/WGMMA/clusters/DSMEM/setmaxnreg; SM100/103 tcgen05/TMEM/2-CTA MMA/cluster launch control; SM120/121 consumer Blackwell with mma.sync only) and by device scale (SM count, L2 size, HBM bandwidth, MIG slices, shared/noisy clocks). Examined: MegaBake's target model (bodies/interface.py TargetFacts, compiler.py _target_facts, runtime.py admit_runtime), provider gating (bodies/gemm.py, bodies/attention.py, bodies/blackwell.py, bodies/catalog.py), launch-policy heuristics (compiler.py, plan.py, schedule.py) and the 2026-10-18 benchmark reports; Mirage MPK (agent_space/mirage python/mirage/mpk, utils.py, tasks/{ampere,hopper,blackwell}); PyTorch Inductor (analysis/device_info.py, heuristics/template/triton.py, utils.py is_big_gpu/decompose_k); TPU megakernels (agent_space/tpu-megakernels); CuTe DSL utilities installed in .venv (hardware_info.py, dynamic_persistent_tile_scheduler.py, blackwell_helpers.py); TileLang Carver (web); Hazy Research megakernel posts (web); CUTLASS CLC docs (web). Question answered: what target abstraction and compile-time selection/autotuning architecture lets MegaBake run well on SM80/SM90/SM100 and on any SM count without baking in constants tuned on the 60-SM H200 MIG slice and the SmolLM/Qwen2 models.

core_ideas.idea: Target facts object queried from the device (not from a name table)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Build one immutable Target record at compile time from cudaGetDeviceProperties/cuDeviceGetAttribute: cc (major, minor, arch-specific suffix a/f), SM count, max smem per block opt-in and per SM, regs per SM/thread, L2 size and persisting-L2 max, max cluster size (cudaOccupancyMaxPotentialClusterSize / HardwareInfo.get_max_active_clusters), memory clock and bus width (theoretical BW), MIG flag/name. Every heuristic reads only this record. TileLang Carver's TileDevice and CuTe DSL HardwareInfo do this; Inductor's DeviceProperties covers SM count/cc/regs but its roofline DeviceInfo is a name-keyed datasheet table that fails for MIG names.
core_ideas.where_in_source: TileLang carver/arch/cuda.py; cutlass/utils/hardware_info.py:28-160; torch/_inductor/runtime/hints.py:217; torch/_inductor/analysis/device_info.py:392-470; MegaBake bodies/interface.py:13-21

core_ideas.idea: Capability flags instead of architecture-string equality
core_ideas.how_it_works: Providers ask for features (has_cp_async, has_tma, has_wgmma, has_tcgen05/TMEM, has_2cta_mma, has_clc, has_dsmem/clusters, has_setmaxnreg, has_pdl, mma_shapes) rather than 'architecture == sm90a'. SM120/121 (consumer Blackwell) has TMA and clusters but no WGMMA and no tcgen05/TMEM, so string groups like 'Blackwell' are wrong. Inductor groups capabilities into classes (sm8x/sm90/sm10x/sm12x) with per-class config tables.

core_ideas.idea: Per-target body/task libraries behind one task contract
core_ideas.how_it_works: Mirage keeps tasks/ampere, tasks/hopper, tasks/blackwell with the same task signature; the Python builder picks a task variant by target_cc and nvcc flags (-DMIRAGE_GRACE_HOPPER / _BLACKWELL, sm_90a / sm_100a). CUTLASS 3.x/CuTe does the same at the collective level: arch tag + MMA atom + copy atom + kernel schedule (KernelTmaWarpSpecializedCooperative, 2SM UMMA) compose into one GemmUniversal. MegaBake's BodyProvider/BodyConfig contract (semantic, layouts, tiles, participants, pipeline, scratch, completion) is already this shape; only the provider set is SM90-centric.
core_ideas.where_in_source: mirage persistent_kernel.py:365-381, :881, :1395-1430; mirage include/.../tasks/{ampere,hopper,blackwell}; MegaBake bodies/interface.py:160-195, bodies/catalog.py:108-150

core_ideas.idea: Analytic roofline cost model per body candidate, calibrated by device microbenchmarks
core_ideas.how_it_works: For each candidate (tile, stages, split-K, swapAB, worker count) compute bytes moved (weights + activations + split-K partials) and FLOPs, then time = max(bytes / (BW_eff(active_SMs)), flops / peak_mma) + waves x per-tile fixed latency + sync cost. BW_eff(active_SMs) is a measured saturation curve (per-SM achievable bandwidth x SMs, capped at device BW), which is what makes split-K and swapAB decisions transferable: on a 132-SM H100 a 2048-wide projection already has 32 tiles < 132 SMs, on 60 SMs it has 32 < 60, so the split-K ratio changes. Calibrate three numbers per device at install time: streaming BW vs active CTAs, grid-barrier/counter latency vs workers, and per-tile pipeline fill latency. TileLang Carver/Roller ranks hints by memory-traffic and tile alignment; Inductor uses datasheet roofline for estimates only; Mirage hardcodes grid sizes per model.
core_ideas.where_in_source: TileLang carver (get_hardware_aware_configs topk); torch/_inductor/analysis/device_info.py datasheet_tops/dram_bw; MegaBake has no cost model (plan.py ranks only by measurement, compiler.py:431 disables measurement for table launches)

core_ideas.idea: Compile-time autotuning restricted to cost-model top-k, measured on device, cached by (target fingerprint, op shape signature) not by model
core_ideas.how_it_works: Search space per GEMM shape: tile (M,N) in a legal set for the MMA family, stages fitting smem, split-K in divisors, swapAB on/off. Cost model prunes to top-k (e.g. 3-5); measure each in a resident-range microbenchmark with rotating weights (cold L2) inside the persistent harness; store results keyed by (cc, SM count, L2, BW class, dtype, M-bucket, N, K). A new model with the same shapes reuses entries; a new GPU re-tunes. Inductor's max-autotune + on-disk cache and CUTLASS profiler follow this pattern; Hazy and Mirage do not autotune (hand-built schedules).
core_ideas.where_in_source: torch/_inductor select_algorithm/autotune cache; MegaBake cache.py:114 (key includes target), plan.py:442-560 (measured search exists but is bypassed for table launches)

core_ideas.idea: Work decomposition derived from SM count (tasks per op, split-K, split-context)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Choose per-op task count so that tasks ~= k x workers with k integer (avoid tail waves) subject to minimum work per task (>= 2 K-tiles in flight, >= 64 keys per attention chunk). Mirage's SM100 split-K picks splits so output_tiles x splits ~= 128 tasks and K/splits is a multiple of 64 for TMA alignment (models/utils.py:17-35); MegaBake's split_k_count already parameterizes by multiprocessor_count. Wave quantization: efficiency = tasks / (ceil(tasks/workers) x workers).

core_ideas.idea: Barrier vs event (counter) synchronization chosen by cost
core_ideas.how_it_works: A grid barrier costs ~T_atomic x log or ~constant (one arrival counter) plus the slowest-CTA skew; per-producer counters cost one release-add per producer task and one acquire-poll per consumer but let independent work start early. Hazy uses per-instruction global counters (and splits the MLP intermediate into 4 counter-chunks); Mirage uses event counters with a scheduler. The choice depends on SM count (barrier skew grows with workers) and on how uneven phases are, so it should be a cost-model decision per interval, not a global mode.
core_ideas.where_in_source: Hazy no-bubbles blog; mirage runtime_header/persistent kernel events; MegaBake runtime.py:66-90, schedule.py (phase vs region-events scheduler), ROADMAP step 10

core_ideas.idea: Shared-memory paging / single smem layout sized from target
core_ideas.how_it_works: Hazy carves the first 213 KB of H100 smem into thirteen 16 KiB pages that instructions request/release, so the next instruction's loads start as pages free. Page count must come from max_smem_per_block_optin (H100/H200 227 KB, B200 228 KB, SM120 ~99 KB, A100 163 KB). MegaBake's table launch uses one fixed 8-stage 64x64 layout (TABLE_GEMM_SHARED_BYTES) that does not fit SM120 or SM86-class parts and is not re-derived per target.

core_ideas.idea: Blackwell-specific: tcgen05 MMA with TMEM accumulators, 2-CTA (cta_group::2) MMA, CLC dynamic scheduling
core_ideas.how_it_works: tcgen05.mma is issued by one thread, reads A/B from smem descriptors and accumulates into Tensor Memory (TMEM, 128 lanes x 512 columns x 32-bit per SM) allocated with tcgen05.alloc; the epilogue reads back with tcgen05.ld. cta_group::2 lets a CTA pair in a cluster compute one 256-row MMA, halving B-operand smem traffic per CTA. Cluster Launch Control (clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel) lets a persistent worker steal not-yet-launched cluster IDs, giving hardware-backed dynamic load balancing that tolerates SMs taken by other work (relevant on shared GPUs). In a megakernel TMEM must be allocated once per CTA lifetime (Mirage allocates per task) and the warp-role structure (TMA warp, MMA warp, epilogue warpgroups) differs from Hopper's producer/consumer warpgroups.
core_ideas.where_in_source: cutlass/utils/blackwell_helpers.py, tmem_allocator.py, dynamic_persistent_tile_scheduler.py; mirage tasks/blackwell/linear_sm100_mpk.cuh:59-572; CUTLASS CLC doc

core_ideas.idea: Hopper-specific: TMA multicast within clusters and distributed shared memory
core_ideas.how_it_works: With clusters, one TMA load multicasts an activation tile to all CTAs of the cluster and DSMEM allows split-K partial reduction through peer smem instead of global memory. Requires cooperative launch with cluster dims; cluster size limits are queried by cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters. MegaBake's gemm.py (CUTLASS-derived) supports multicast but the table launch uses cluster (1,1).

core_ideas.idea: Ampere fallback path: cp.async multistage + mma.sync
core_ideas.how_it_works: SM80/86/89 have no TMA/WGMMA; GEMM bodies use cp.async.cg 16-byte copies into a multi-stage smem ring with ldmatrix + mma.sync.m16n8k16. Mirage keeps tasks/ampere; Inductor keeps sm8x configs; Hazy notes CUDA-core paths can beat tensor cores for batch-1 GEMV on Hopper. For decode GEMV-like shapes, a bandwidth-bound cp.async GEMV body is enough to reach ~80-90% of HBM on SM80.

Grid barrier, event counters, work tables, phase tables, TMA-descriptor-in-prologue, address tables and verification are target-independent given (a) cooperative launch or CLC and (b) gpu-scope acquire/release atomics, available SM70+. Only body providers and the smem/register budget need per-target code.
core_ideas.where_in_source: MegaBake runtime.py, schedule.py, codegen.py table module; ROADMAP.md:106-108

core_ideas.how_it_works: A MIG slice reports its own SM count (60 for H200 3g.71gb) and a proportional L2 and HBM share, but device name strings do not match datasheet tables (Inductor lookup misses), and clocks/bandwidth vary with neighbours. Tuning must therefore use measured bandwidth for the slice, record noise (median + IQR), and use a tie tolerance; cooperative grids must be sized from occupancy queries at runtime. CLC on Blackwell is the hardware answer to SMs being unavailable.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Whole-model joint work decomposition against a single SM budget
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: In one persistent kernel the compiler sees every op's task count and can choose split-K/tiles so that concurrently-ready ops in one barrier interval jointly fill exactly W workers (e.g. q,k,v projections with 32 tiles each plus an attention tail). Separate kernels each pick a grid independently (cuBLAS heuristics per call); concurrency across kernels needs multiple streams and the hardware block scheduler, which a CUDA graph can express but cannot co-tile.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: Horizontal fusion (Inductor combo kernels / grouped GEMM) for sibling ops, or stream-parallel graph branches; recovers part of the fill but not cross-op pipelining.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Hardware-portable dynamic scheduling via CLC or counters inside one launch
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: A megakernel can use one persistent work queue (counters, or CLC on SM100) spanning all ops, so SMs lost to MIG neighbours or skew rebalance across ops. Per-kernel CLC only balances within one kernel; the inter-kernel boundary is still a full drain.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: PDL (programmatic dependent launch) overlaps the next kernel's prologue with the previous tail; it cannot start dependent tiles of the next op before the whole previous grid signals.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Cross-op L2/smem prefetch planned with known L2 size
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: Knowing the next op's weights and the L2 size of the target, idle CTAs at a barrier can issue cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 for the next GEMM's tiles; the size budget is a target fact (29 MiB MIG slice vs 50 MiB H100 vs 126 MiB B200 class). Separate kernels can only prefetch within their own lifetime; PDL prologues can prefetch a little but the previous kernel's SMs are still busy.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: PDL + cudaGridDependencySynchronize with an early prefetch in the dependent kernel prologue; partial overlap.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Single register/smem/TMEM budget allocated once for the whole model
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: TMEM allocation (tcgen05.alloc), barrier init, TMA descriptor prefetch and setmaxnreg warp-role layout can be done once per CTA lifetime and amortized over every layer; separate kernels pay them per launch.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: None equivalent; CUDA graphs remove CPU cost but not per-kernel device prologue/epilogue.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multi_kernel_cannot: A kernel boundary is always a full barrier; only a megakernel can replace it with per-tile counters where the cost model says so (e.g. more SMs => more barrier skew => counters pay off more on 132/148-SM parts than on 60).
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multi_kernel_substitute: Stream-K / persistent fused kernels per block, PDL.

expected_impact_on_megabake: [uncertain] Ranking, for H200 MIG 3g.71gb, decode at batch 1. Baseline: 1.7B decode kernel 2.97 ms = ~1.92 ms GEMM at ~1.78 TB/s + ~1.0 ms non-GEMM (49 RMSNorm ~5 us, 24 attention ~10 us, ~6 barrier intervals/layer x 24 layers x ~0.7 us ~= 0.1 ms raw barrier cost plus per-interval latency tails). Weight-stream roofline at 2.2 TB/s ~= 1.55 ms. (1) Per-GEMM cost-model selection of split-K and swapAB (instead of launch-wide booleans and an env flag): 2048-wide projections give 32 weight tiles on 60 SMs (53% fill); split-K 2 lifts fill to ~100%. If o_proj/down_proj/k/v GEMMs move from ~1.78 toward ~2.0 TB/s, GEMM time drops ~0.15-0.25 ms (5-8% of kernel) [uncertain until measured]. (2) Cost-model-driven barrier vs counter per interval (needs ROADMAP step 10): removes part of the ~0.7 us x ~144 intervals plus skew; ~0.1-0.3 ms on 1.7B [uncertain]. (3) Target-derived smem budget and stage count: no change on H200 (already 227 KB), but prevents silent fallback to generic bodies on SM120/SM80-class parts (10-40x slower GEMMs there). (4) Real SM100 provider (tcgen05/TMEM, TMA, CLC): zero effect on the H200 test box; on B200 it is the difference between a usable and an unusable compiler, since the current mma.sync body has no smem pipeline and would likely run at well under 30% of HBM bandwidth [uncertain, not measured]. (5) Per-shape tuning database + top-k measurement: compile-time cost (first call is ~21 s today) should fall for repeat shapes and rise moderately for new shapes; runtime gain is the sum of (1) plus tile choices, mostly via preventing regressions on new models. Prefill (128-300 tokens, 3-21x slower than Inductor): the main lever is a cost-model-chosen non-swapAB large-M tile set (64x128/128x128, cluster multicast) per GEMM instead of the launch-wide 64x64 8-stage table layout; this could recover several-fold on prefill GEMMs [uncertain], but it is a provider/tiling issue more than a target-abstraction issue.
generality_and_overfitting_risk: Model-generic vs tuned: (a) compiler.py:431 forces SearchBudget(max_plans=1) for every table launch, so every real model runs on rule-picked bodies with no measurement - rules were derived on SmolLM-135M/1.7B and Qwen2-0.5B; any new model shape (e.g. N not a multiple of 64, GQA ratio, head_dim 256) gets no corrective search. (b) bodies/gemm.py:1888-1905: SWAP_AB_MAX_ROWS=64, SWAP_AB_ROW_TILES=(16,32,64), SPLIT_K_MAX=16, SPLIT_K_MIN_K_TILES=2; the comment cites 60-SM bandwidth numbers. wants_swap_ab (gemm.py:1992) is all-or-nothing per launch, so one large-M GEMM (e.g. a vision tower or a long-prefill bucket) flips every GEMM's orientation - a shape-mix overfit. (c) gemm.py:1711 TABLE_GEMM_SHARED_BYTES and gemm.py:1879-1881 literal smem sizes (230400, 214016) and stage counts (13, 8) assume 227 KB smem (H100/H200/B200 only). (d) gemm.py:2232 evidence 'max_admitted_workers': 60 and microsecond timings measured on the MIG slice are stored as body evidence. (e) attention.py:422-423 DECODE_MAX_CHUNKS=16, DECODE_MIN_CHUNK_KEYS=64 fixed rather than derived from SMs x heads x KV length. (f) schedule.py:1384-1386 folding limits (2/6/6 'rounds') stand in for a latency model; on a 132-SM part barriers cost more and folding should be more aggressive, on SM80 less. (g) generic.py:441,478 elements-per-thread 4, unroll 16, and catalog.py:132 128 threads for every target. (h) compiler.py:205-210 table-launch thresholds are CUDA ABI-driven (32 KiB params) - generic, fine. (i) compiler.py:236-248 tolerances justified by SmolLM-1.7B observations - model-derived numbers. (j) runtime.py:265 plan rejects any device with a different SM count: correct but means a cached plan is per-slice. Hardware-generic: providers check architecture strings (gemm.py:1847, attention.py:220) - every non-sm90a target loses tuned GEMM and attention entirely; blackwell.py lumps SM100 (tcgen05) with SM120 (no tcgen05) and registers a weak common-denominator body. How references avoid (or fail to avoid) this: Inductor - capability-class config tables plus max-autotune measurement and on-disk cache, smem fit checked against shared_memory_per_block_optin; but it also overfits (is_big_gpu >= 68 SMs disables its GEMM autotune on the 60-SM slice; decompose-K split list is 'hand-tuned'; datasheet table keyed by name misses MIG). Mirage - per-arch task libraries but grid sizes are per-model literals ('96 and 64 are enough to cover all Qwen3 model?', models/utils.py:4) and worker count from an SM-count step table (utils.py:33-53), split-K only on cc==100 (qwen3/builder.py:293). TPU megakernels - vmem_limit 64 MiB and 'B8 optimum on TPU v6e' literals. TileLang Carver - queries SM count, smem, L2 from device; ranks top-k hints analytically; but bandwidth is a placeholder constant. Hazy - hand-written per-model instruction sets; no generality claim. Conclusion: no reference system is fully generic; the robust pattern is device-queried facts + analytic pruning + small measured search + target/shape-keyed cache, and MegaBake should adopt that rather than copy any reference's constants.
hardware_portability: SM90-only today: WGMMA mainloop and swapAB (bodies/gemm.py), TMA descriptors written in the table-launch prologue (codegen.py), setmaxnreg warp-role changes (PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:287), WGMMA attention (attention.py:220), cluster plumbing. Carries to SM100/103: TMA (same descriptors), clusters/multicast, DSMEM, PDL, cooperative launch, gpu-scope atomics, grid barrier, event counters, table launch; must be rewritten: MMA (WGMMA -> tcgen05.mma single-thread issue, accumulators in TMEM, tcgen05.ld epilogue, TMEM alloc once per CTA lifetime), warp roles (TMA warp / MMA warp / epilogue warpgroups), optional 2-CTA MMA (cluster pairs, which constrains the cooperative grid to even CTA counts and cluster-aligned work), CLC as an alternative to static persistent ranges. SM120/121: TMA and clusters but mma.sync (no WGMMA, no tcgen05), ~99-100 KB smem - needs smaller stage counts and the Ampere-style mainloop with TMA loads. SM80/86/89: cp.async + ldmatrix + mma.sync, no TMA, no clusters; table launch must pass global pointers instead of TMA descriptors; cooperative launch and atomics are fine. Keep it target-generic by: capability flags, one BodyConfig contract per op family with per-target providers, smem/register/TMEM budgets derived from queried facts, and runtime pieces that never mention an architecture. Grid barrier latency and its scaling with SM count must be measured per device, not assumed 0.7 us.
